CONTEXT SWITCHBOARD — BEGINNER EXPERIMENT PROTOCOL
Prepared 25 October 2026. Status: proposed, not executed.

PURPOSE
Determine when an agent needs more input, when extra input interferes, and
whether selecting or separating applicable context improves its actions.
The output should identify the next engineering intervention, not merely
declare one context size a winner.

SCOPE
Context means the instructions, question, source blocks and tool definitions
supplied to the model for the current task. Every rollout starts fresh.
No persistent memory, cross-session learning, retention policy, model training,
or external-history retrieval is part of this study. Selection operates only
over the task's supplied source packet.

RESEARCH QUESTION
Can a bounded-context agent correctly apply rules to their intended target
when closely related but inapplicable rules appear in the same source packet?

PROPOSED CONTRIBUTION AND NOVELTY STATUS
The candidate contribution is a paired relevance-reversal evaluation of scope
binding: the same packet supports two independent tasks; a rule useful for A
is inapplicable to B and vice versa. Combine action-level grading, token-budget
controls, and evidence-coverage diagnostics.
This is not a verified first-ever experiment. Position, distraction, and
instruction confusion have prior work. Compare the exact task generator and
claims against DIM-Bench, GSM-DC and LURCH before asserting novelty. A focused
search is not an exhaustive novelty proof. If the same design exists, frame
the work as replication and extension or revise the contribution.

HYPOTHESES
H1: At complete evidence coverage, similar-but-inapplicable rules produce more
wrong-scope actions than equal-length unrelated material.
H2: Grouping already-present facts and scope labels reduces these errors at
matched token count. It must not add scope information missing in the baseline.
H3: Scope-aware selection outperforms scope-blind lexical selection under a
fixed input cap, provided it preserves all required evidence.
These are untested predictions. Null or reversed results are valid outcomes.

TASK
An event assistant receives an explicit target team, room options, scoped
requirements and shared booking rules. It must call book_room(room_id), or
report infeasibility when no room satisfies all applicable constraints.
The tool is a local simulation: no real booking occurs.
Begin with one action decision; later extend to several decisions with
externally controlled, identical observations. Fresh independent decisions
are sufficient for the first context study; do not equate it with a full
long-horizon agent benchmark.

GENERATOR
Generate structured ground truth before rendering natural language. Each
packet contains two targets with different valid solutions, plausible rules
for other targets, shared requirements and available options. Give every
block an ID and visible scope label. Gold answers and minimal sufficient
evidence sets are evaluator-only fields.
Make the constraint solver enumerate valid actions deterministically. Avoid
ambiguous ties or specify a tie-break rule. Include a small balanced set of
infeasible cases so the model cannot always succeed by booking something.
Randomize names, values, source order and answer position. Do not mark distractors
with special words. Use multiple independently written language templates.
All conditions receive the same visible metadata. Never label a block with
its gold relevance for the particular question.

SIX POLICIES
1. Full-flat: all source blocks and original labels, in interleaved order.
2. Full-grouped: identical blocks and labels grouped by target/shared scope.
3. Limited-recent: last whole blocks fitting the input budget.
4. Limited-lexical: BM25-ranked whole blocks from the source packet.
5. Limited-scoped: filter explicit target/shared scope, then use the same BM25
   implementation and packing rule. Target parsing must use the visible query,
   not gold labels. Start with exact target names; test aliases separately.
6. Oracle diagnostic: evaluator supplies a minimal sufficient evidence set.
   This is privileged and not deployable. If no sufficient set fits, mark the
   oracle condition infeasible at that budget; do not secretly exceed it.

Full versus limited is an end-to-end input-policy comparison, not a pure
causal estimate of length. Policies differ in exposed evidence and ordering.
Use the interventions below to identify the relevant mechanisms.

CONTROLLED INTERVENTIONS
A. Information presence: remove one required fact and substitute equal-length
   unrelated text. Restore it in a rescue condition.
B. Interference: hold necessary facts fixed and replace unrelated padding with
   similar but explicitly other-target rules at the same token count.
C. Position: move identical required evidence to start, middle or end.
D. Structure: group versus interleave identical labeled blocks. Match token
   counts with tokenizer-verified serialization and counterbalanced separators.
E. Relevance reversal: independently query the two targets on the same packet.
   Reset model and tool state between tasks. Do not expose the other answer.

Avoid making every condition a giant factorial at first. Run the core six
policies, then choose one intervention based on diagnosed failures. If changing
separators or padding affects meaning, record it and add a padding control;
token matching alone does not make two prompts semantically identical.

BUDGETS AND RUN CONTROLS
Pilot limited input budget: 2,000 tokens total, including system instructions,
question, tool schema, source blocks and any protocol overhead. Use the chosen
model's actual tokenizer or verified API token counter. Reserve output
separately, initially 512 tokens, and document the provider's accounting.
All full packets must fit the selected model's native window including output.
Reject or resize oversized packets; never silently truncate the full baseline.
Ensure some full packets exceed the limited cap, otherwise the test is trivial.
Freeze model/version, system prompt, decoding settings, tool interface and
maximum action calls. Start with one action call; malformed outputs count as
failures. Permit no hidden retries. Later recovery trials use the same call
budget for all methods. Account for every selector/model call in total cost.
The corpus and its blocks are the same across practical policies. The oracle
alone uses gold evidence. A selector may read the whole task packet, which is
selection-stage access, not a small end-to-end information budget. State this
explicitly and count preprocessing time/cost.

PILOT AND CONFIRMATION
Pilot: six packet pairs, 12 tasks, six policies, one repetition = 72 rollouts.
Use the pilot to catch task ambiguity, trivial success, and scoring bugs.
Do not report the pilot as a reliable comparison.
Provisional next stage: 60 fresh packet pairs x two targets x six policies x
three repetitions = 2,160 rollouts. This is a planning size, not a power claim.
Use pilot variance and a predeclared smallest meaningful difference to choose
the final sample size before examining held-out results.
Randomize condition execution order. Keep development templates separate from
held-out templates; split by packet pair, not by individual query.

MEASUREMENTS
Primary: action success satisfying every applicable constraint.
Secondary:
- wrong-scope action rate, based on the deterministic constraint checker;
- required-evidence coverage before the model answers;
- success conditional on complete coverage (descriptive, not alone causal);
- position/constraint-type breakdowns;
- actual input/output tokens per call and total across the pipeline;
- selector overhead, API cost with date/version/pricing, cache treatment;
- end-to-end latency and tool/schema errors.
An action is classified as wrong-scope-compatible when it violates a target
constraint while matching a competing target's corresponding rule. This does
not reveal the model's hidden reasoning. Use controlled scope changes to
strengthen attribution. An action may violate several constraints; preserve
multi-label diagnostics as well as any preregistered exclusive classification.
If multiple minimal sufficient evidence sets exist, count coverage of any one
complete valid set rather than requiring one arbitrary annotation.

ANALYSIS
Compare methods on the same packets. Report paired success differences with
95% confidence intervals clustered by packet pair, keeping paired targets and
repetitions together in resampling. Do not treat repeats as new independent
tasks. Predeclare the primary contrast and label other comparisons exploratory;
adjust for multiple comparisons when making confirmatory claims.
For equivalence or non-inferiority, specify a practical margin before testing
(for example, 3 percentage points if justified by the product). A nonsignificant
difference is not evidence that methods are equal.
Also show success versus total cost. A smaller prompt is not necessarily a
cheaper pipeline. Keep no-fit/oracle-infeasible cases visible in coverage reports.

DECISION RULES FOR ITERATION
Limited wins with coverage intact -> test interference and optimize selection.
Limited loses and misses evidence -> improve coverage or raise the budget;
  perform equal-length evidence restoration before blaming reasoning.
Complete evidence but wrong-scope-compatible actions -> test grouping and
  applicability labels with identical facts and matched token counts.
Oracle also fails -> audit task correctness, simplify reasoning depth, check
  tool use, and then consider a stronger model in a separate experiment.
Methods look similar -> inspect task difficulty and uncertainty. Expand only
  according to the prespecified plan; use a valid non-inferiority test before
  preferring a cheaper policy on quality-equivalence grounds.
Benefits disappear on transfer -> limit claims and improve generalization;
  do not tune on the held-out test set.

LATER VARIABLES
Input cap (1k/2k/4k), distractor similarity, evidence placement and dispersion,
number of dependent constraints, exact versus compressed wording, tool-schema
volume, metadata quality, aliases, and an independently held-out second domain.
Use a constant answering model first. A model comparison is a separate axis.
Do not introduce memory as an explanation or intervention.

FIRST PRODUCT COMPONENT
A context assembler that takes the current request and source packet, selects
applicable blocks under a budget, preserves scope/provenance, and logs the exact
model input. Its next change should follow observed failures, not complexity
for its own sake.
